findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or describe permissions (and anyone with repository access) can read these long-lived static credentials.

The function's environment variables are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (no kms_key_arn set), so the sensitive values are protected only by the AWS-managed default key and are visible in the console/API to any principal with describe access.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package is not signature-validated before execution, allowing tampered artefacts between build and deployment to run undetected.
The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group controls, providing an unmonitored data exfiltration path.
